sources.locator: §1 printed pp. 1-3, §2 printed pp. 3-7, §3 printed pp. 7-9, §4 printed pp. 9-12 (relativity, intervals, proper time, Lorentz transformation), §16-§17 printed pp. 44-49 (four-potential and equations of motion), §23 printed pp. 60-62 (the electromagnetic field tensor), §26 printed pp. 66-67 and §28-§30 printed pp. 69-75 (the two pairs of Maxwell's equations, the four-current and continuity), §6-§7 and §9 printed pp. 14-28 (four-vectors, four-velocity, energy-momentum); read in the stamped 387-page full text (Gaussian-unit conventions re-expressed in the framework's SI conventions).

contents.name: §1-§4: the relativity principle with propagation velocity c, Minkowski coordinates, intervals, proper time and Lorentz transformations
contents.support: The restricted inertial chart, its time coordinate x^0 = ct, the constant future unit time vector and the frame-dependent spatial structure are the library's exact formulation of this coordinate structure; also the geometric part of post-em-minkowski-physical-model.

contents.name: §6-§7 and §9: four-vectors, four-velocity and the energy-momentum four-vector
contents.support: The definitions of four-velocity and the worldline objects are consumed from the in-run SR items; this source backs the general four-vector conventions, not a dynamical claim.

contents.name: §16-§17: the four-potential A^i = (phi, A) and the equations of motion of a charge in a field
contents.support: The adopted covariant coupling m dU/dtau = q Phi(U) and the exclusion of the self-field follow the source's equation-of-motion discussion; the SI normalization and the index form are the library's.

contents.name: §23: F_ik = dA_k/dx^i - dA_i/dx^k, the electromagnetic field tensor and its E,H components
contents.support: Clause (a) of the definition fixes the same component dictionary (F_0i = -E_i/c, F_ij = eps_ijk B_k) in the (-+++) conventions; clause (c) is the source's potential identity.

contents.name: §26 and §30: the first and second pairs of Maxwell's equations, and §28-§29: the four-current j^i = (c rho, j) and the equation of continuity
contents.support: The four equations adopted in the smooth branch are the source's two pairs re-expressed in SI units; the four-current and its continuity are the interface consumed by def-em-sources.

contents.name: §5 (transformation of velocities and the light-speed bound), §8, §10-§15 (mechanics and collisions), Chapters 5-15 (constant fields, waves, radiation, gravitation)
contents.reason: The velocity bound and mechanics are supplied by the in-run SR pages; constant-field solutions, plane waves, radiation and the gravitational chapters belong to the later physics pages (electrostatics, waves, retarded fields) of this framework and are not prerequisites of the primitives page.

contents.name: The Gaussian-unit normalization of all field equations
contents.reason: The framework adopts SI; this source's unit normalization is not copied, only the equation structure and the tensor definitions.

contents.name: §7.3.3 printed pp. 326-327: the four Maxwell equations (7.39) in SI, the force law (7.40) and the continuity equation (7.41)
contents.support: The exact SI constants and signs of the four equations adopted in the smooth branch; the source's warning that the equations require boundary conditions is retained in the statement's scope.

contents.name: §7.3.4 printed p. 327: the magnetic-charge terms are set to zero
contents.support: The postulate's clause (c) (no magnetic charge) follows the source's discussion; the source's mono-pole literature references are not part of the item.

contents.name: §5.1.2 printed pp. 204-205: F = Q[E + (v x B)], stated as a fundamental axiom, and B as a pseudovector
contents.support: The adopted coupling and the polar/axial convention of def-em-fields; the source's Newtonian equation F = m rddot is not adopted as exact.

contents.name: §5.3.2 printed pp. 224-225: mu_0 = 4pi x 10^-7 N/A^2 and 1 T = 1 N/(A m)
contents.support: Only the unit identity 1 T = 1 N/(A m) is used; the pre-2019 exact value of mu_0 printed by this edition is expressly not adopted as exact (the SI brochure's measured status controls).

contents.name: §12.1-§12.2 and §12.3.1 printed pp. 491-531: inertial frames, proper time, four-vectors and the field tensor F^{mu nu} in terms of E and B
contents.support: The component dictionary and the invariant structure; the library's index/sign choices are stated explicitly and differ from the source only by the documented optional magnetic sign.

contents.name: §1.5 printed pp. 45-52: the one- and three-dimensional delta function as a distribution defined by evaluation
contents.support: The source's caution that the delta is not a function backs the example's contrast; the non-representation statement is proved locally in the example from the cutoff lemma and Riemann-integral tools, not cited from this source.

contents.name: §7.3.5-§7.3.6 and Chapters 4, 6 (matter equations, boundary conditions, dielectrics, magnets)
contents.reason: Constitutive laws and interface conditions are the later material-response page's subject.

contents.name: Chapters 8-11 (conservation laws, potentials, radiation, electrodynamics and relativity applications)
contents.reason: Energy-momentum balance, potentials and gauge, retarded fields and radiation are later pages of this framework; the primitives page stops at definitions and postulates.

canonical.name: Restricted inertial chart, slices and fixed-time laboratory fields

canonical.name: Charge parameter, smooth frame densities, volume charge, flux and the four-current
canonical.support: Both the compact-Jordan Riemann charge and full bounded-Lebesgue-measurable charge are retained. Exact pinned boundedness/measurability/finite-measure/integral suppliers prove the measurable charge finite under explicitly scoped Countable Choice. General scalar multiplier and separately normalized material four-velocity branches have distinct exact frame-density equality cases.

canonical.name: Electric and magnetic fields as fixed-time spatial vector fields with a stated regularity class
canonical.support: Locally assembled from Tong §1.2, Griffiths §1.1-§1.2 and the standard polar/axial convention; no field equation is asserted.

canonical.name: Adopted physical Minkowski model with inertial descriptions, ideal clocks and ideal light
canonical.support: Locally assembled as an adopted postulate from the run's SR postulates and the mathematical Minkowski model; the exposition separates what the model fixes from what is adopted.

canonical.name: Worldlines, four-velocity, chart readings and the frame/observer distinction
canonical.support: Locally assembled from the run's SR curve, proper-time and observer items; the definitions are reused with their exact statements rather than restated.

canonical.name: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations in smooth and weak branches
canonical.support: Locally assembled from LL §§26 and 30, Tong §1.2.1 and Griffiths §7.3.3 in the SI conventions of the SI brochure; the weak branch is stated with the published distribution interface and singular sources are excluded.

canonical.name: The electromagnetic two-form, its observer decomposition and the four-current interface
canonical.support: The adopted F0i=-Ei/c,Fij=epsilonijk Bk and qPhi force convention are preserved. Observer e=+E/c,b=-B gives the corrected dual/wedge invariants. The SR optional tensor is the negative of the entire tensor. C1 potential closure is proved using compact test integration by parts twice and mixed derivatives of smooth tests, without C2 narrowing.

canonical.name: Superposition for finitely many prescribed Maxwell fields and sources
canonical.support: The K1 conditional argument: linearity of divergence, curl and the time derivative in both branches; the nonlinear-source and infinite-superposition exclusions are part of the statement.

canonical.name: The Lorentz coupling: covariant test-charge equation and continuum force and power densities
canonical.support: Locally assembled from Tong §1.2, Griffiths §5.1.2 and §8.1.1 and LL §§17 and 23 in the run's SI and index conventions; self-fields, radiation reaction and any exact Newtonian law are excluded.

canonical.name: Full measurable-volume charge with retained compact-Jordan comparison
canonical.support: Local exact bounded-density/finite-measure proof from pinned mathematical suppliers, with AComega only on that Lebesgue interface. No convergence theorem or extra Choice assumption is invented.

canonical.name: C1 potential closure by compact smooth-test cancellation
canonical.support: Complete local twofold integration-by-parts proof using earlier choice-free compact-variation/fundamental lemma and pinned Clairaut-Schwarz on smooth tests only; continuous cyclic derivative vanishes pointwise. No second classical potential derivatives are presumed.
